arguments.claim: The right of everyone charged with a criminal offence to be effectively defended by a lawyer is a fundamental feature of a fair trial; suspects should have access to legal assistance from the moment of police custody.

anchor.surface_text: The Court reiterates that the right of everyone charged with a criminal offence to be effectively defended by a lawyer, assigned officially if need be, is one of the fundamental features of a fair trial (see Salduz, cited above, § 51; Poitrimol v. France, 23 November 1993, § 34, Series A no. 277-A; and Demebukov v. Bulgaria, no. 68020/01, § 50, 28 February 2008). The Court is of the view that the fairness of criminal proceedings under Article 6 of the Convention requires that, as a rule, a suspect should be granted access to legal assistance from the moment he is taken into police custody or pre-trial detention.

arguments.court_reasoning: The Court applied established case-law (Salduz and others) confirming the fundamental right to legal assistance from police custody.

arguments.claim: An accused person is entitled, as soon as taken into custody, to be assisted by a lawyer, not only while being questioned, to secure fundamental aspects of defence including discussion, evidence collection, preparation, support, and detention conditions.

anchor.surface_text: In accordance with the generally recognised international norms, which the Court accepts and which form the framework for its case-law, an accused person is entitled, as soon as he or she is taken into custody, to be assisted by a lawyer, and not only while being questioned (for the relevant international legal materials see Salduz, cited above, §§ 37-44). Indeed, the fairness of proceedings requires that an accused be able to obtain the whole range of services specifically associated with legal assistance. In this regard, counsel has to be able to secure without restriction the fundamental aspects of that person’s defence: discussion of the case, organisation of the defence, collection of evidence favourable to the accused, preparation for questioning, support of an accused in distress and checking of the conditions of detention.

2.  Holds that there has been a violation of Article 6 § 3 (c) of the Convention taken in conjunction with Article 6 § 1 on account of the fact that the applicant did not have any legal assistance while in police custody;

3.  Holds that there has been a violation of Article 6 § 1 of the Convention on account of the non-communication to the applicant, before the Court of Cassation, of the written submissions of the Principal Public Prosecutor;

4.  Holds

(a)  that the respondent State is to pay the applicant, within three months from the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, EUR 1,000 (one thousand euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable, in respect of non-pecuniary damage, to be converted into Turkish liras at the rate applicable at the date of settlement;
5.  Dismisses the remainder of the applicant’s claim for just satisfaction.
